title: [Chapitre] VII. Analysis situs (troisième mouture) : notes manuscrites (23-26/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (Analysis situs, 3rd version, 1986). M is a set of 'pieces' carrying a symmetric disjointness relation X ∥ Y. For A ⊂ M:
- cosupp A = C_M(A) = {X ∈ M | X ∥ Y for all Y ∈ A}.
- supp A = C_M(C_M(A)), the biorthogonal (bipolar) closure.
- The supports Σ_M are the closed sets A = supp A.

Each X has a realization |X| ⊂ P (P is a set of 'points'). Condition (iii)_M says X ∥ Y ⇔ |X| ∩ |Y| = ∅. Put |A| = ∪_{X∈A} |X|.

On p.75 he wanted the equivalence (*): supp A ⊂ supp B ⇔ |A| ⊂ |B|. He showed the left side is equivalent to: for all X, |X|∩|B| = ∅ ⇒ |X|∩|A| = ∅. That gives ⇐, but the converse is unclear in general.

This page:
1. If B is a support, the left side of (*) means A ⊂ B, because supp is a closure operator. This trivially gives |A| ⊂ |B|.
2. Lemma: under (iii)_M alone, |A| ⊂ |B| ⇒ supp A ⊂ supp B. Here supp A ⊂ supp B is equivalent to A ⊂ supp B. The converse holds when B is a support.
3. Corollary: the map Σ_M → 𝔓(P), A ↦ |A|, is injective, and inclusion of supports is the inclusion induced from 𝔓(P). So the complete lattice of supports order-embeds into the power set of P.
4. He then asks how the lattice operations behave. The meet ∧A_i is the intersection ∩A_i (an intersection of closed sets is closed). The join ∨A_i is supp(∪A_i). One has tautologically |∧A_i| ⊂ ∩|A_i| and |∨A_i| ⊃ ∪|A_i|, but he doubts equality holds in general.
5. He claims |C_M(A)| ⊂ P∖|A|. This is proved on p.77, which then isolates a separation hypothesis (every x ∉ |A| lies in some |X| with X ∥ A) that would make everything work.

Purpose: build a 'point-set' (set-theoretic) model for an abstract, piece-based tame topology, in which supports behave like closed subsets of P.
errors: No errors. All the stated inclusions and the lemma are correct.
His doubts are justified: equality in the meet/join formulas and in |C_M(A)| = P∖|A| genuinely fails without an extra separation hypothesis, which he introduces on p.77.
Minor: p.77's transcription writes P∖A where P∖|A| is meant.

ideas.what: Supports as biorthogonally closed sets for a disjointness relation; meet is intersection, join is the closure of the union, C_M is the orthocomplement
ideas.modern_name: Galois connection / polarity of an orthogonality space; complete ortholattice of closed subsets
ideas.where_published: Not in published texts; tame topology is only sketched programmatically in Esquisse d'un programme (1984)

ideas.what: Order-embedding of the lattice of supports into 𝔓(P) via the realization A ↦ |A|
ideas.modern_name: Representation of a closure lattice by point sets (a disjointness-preserving set representation)

ideas.what: Failure of |·| to preserve meets and joins without a separation hypothesis
ideas.modern_name: Non-distributivity / non-preservation of lattice operations by a set representation

missed.claim: Grothendieck's axiomatics of 'pieces' with a disjointness relation and biorthogonal supports is essentially the theory of orthogonality spaces / ortholattices from quantum logic. He apparently develops it independently as a foundation for analysis situs (tame topology), a link not made in the literature on his tame topology program.
missed.quote: Qu'en est-il de l'intersection ⋀_i (=⋂_i) et de sup ⋁_i des supports?
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Only mildly. It situates his unpublished tame-topology foundations relative to orthogonality-space and o-minimal frameworks, but the mathematics on this page is elementary.

deep.surprise_reason: The page carries elementary closure-operator / Galois-connection lemmas inside an unpublished foundational attempt at tame topology. It is historically interesting as part of the 1986 Analysis situs notes but mathematically routine.
transcription_corrections: '(ici_M)' is likely '(iii_M)', i.e. condition (iii) relative to M, as in p.75's '(iii)'.
The '⇕ (A ⊂ supp B)' line expresses an equivalence with the left-hand side supp A ⊂ supp B, not with |A| ⊂ |B|.
